title: Capacity probing sprint digest — week of 2026-06-30
content:
Purpose

This is the weekly synth for the capacity-probing sprint (runbook prototyping + small-batch experiments) covering the period 2026-06-24 to 2026-06-30. Goal: surface what we observed from priming/pre-warm experiments, small regional failures, and quick decisions for next-week runbook alignment. This is a working note — expect follow-ups and a cleaned playbook draft next week.

Attendees (core):
- Aisha Patel (owner)
- Marco Rivera (fleet ops)
- Jin Park (serving-runtime)
- Emilia Novak (SRE — regions)
- Trevor Huang (capacity modeling)
- plus ad-hoc: product-hosted-api and on-call engineers for short windows

High-level summary / takeaways
1) Priming window tuning reduced tail-latency spikes in APAC by ~14% for the measured workload mix (short-chat + embeddings). The approach that worked was time-bound priming (5–12 minute window after a slot becomes idle) + capped KV warm cache reuse.
2) Pre-warm A/B: conservative pre-warm (allocate ephemeral slot at 25% probability for slots expected to see traffic in next 10 minutes) improved coldstart failures but increased short-term cost by ~2.6%. We have an acceptable tradeoff path for bursty customers if we can route only 20% of burst traffic through pre-warmed lanes.
3) EU-wide cloud maintenance on Jun 27 produced a ~3-hour class of transient errors for dedicated pools. Our cross-region fallback routing recovered most requests but degraded to a cheaper model variant — acceptable for latency-tolerant workloads but not for pinned SLAs.
4) Action: add explicit pinned-capacity guardrail in the Dedicated allocation flow and update the console alerting so customers are aware before maintenance windows.

Detailed experiment notes
Experiment A — Adaptive priming windows (APAC edge focus)\- Period: 2026-06-25 02:00–2026-06-28 23:00 UTC\- Configs tested: fixed priming windows (2m, 5m, 10m); adaptive window based on recent request inter-arrival quantiles (Q90 -> 5m, Q95 -> 10m).\- Observations: adaptive windows achieved the best balance. For our short-chat production traces, adaptive avoided unnecessary warmups during idle tails but caught 78% of short bursts that previously caused cold KV cache misses. Latency p95 fell 14% compared to baseline; cost delta was +0.9% due to a small number of long warm sessions.\- Notes: adaptive logic needs a lower-bound floor (2m) to avoid thrash for ultra-bursty micro-patterns.

Experiment B — Probabilistic pre-warm lanes (controlled A/B)\- Period: 2026-06-26 08:00–2026-06-29 20:00 UTC\- Idea: pre-warm ephemeral slots probabilistically for high-likelihood routing keys (derived from recent user-session histories).\- Results: at 25% probability we saw a 45% reduction in errors labeled as "cold-kv+timeout" on short tails; token cost for the fleet rose 2.6%. At 50% probability the cost rose ~6% with diminishing latency returns.\- Conclusion: 25% pre-warm with routing to cost-aware lanes gives best marginal ROI. Need to pair with per-customer opt-in or tier gating in Console (product asks).

Incident note — EU maintenance (Jun 27)\- Cloud provider announced node IM maintenance for eu-west-1; several dedicated pools lost a set of node leases for ~90 minutes, then re-provisioning followed for another ~60–90 min.\- What happened: our primary dedicated pools in eu-west-1 lost capacity abruptly; smart routing initiated cross-region fallback to eu-central and us-west; fallback used a cheaper quantized model variant due to compatibility constraints.\- Impact: ~1.8% reduction in successful low-latency responses for enterprise customers pinned to dedicated (escalations opened). Revenue impact minimal for hosted customers (auto-fallback present), but alerted priority sales/CS.\- Immediate remediation: manual rebalancing of reserved slots and invoking emergency warmup for pinned tenants.

Capacity snapshot (end-of-week):
- Total provisioned GPU slots (fleet): 11,820\- Idle buffer (global) nominal: 6.1% (target 5–8%)\- APAC edge spare: 3.2% (below target) — we saw the APAC priming experiment finish with improved tail but still constrained spare slots during the evening window (UTC+8 peak).\- EU dedicated pools: average utilization 88% during maintenance windows (higher than expected).

Operational decisions and runbook changes
- Add a "pinned-capacity guardrail" flag in the Dedicated control-plane that prevents automated cross-region fallback for workloads marked DONT-FALLBACK unless a manual override is set. (Owner: Jin Park, JIRA-INFRA-2148, due 2026-07-07)
- Console notification: expose scheduled cloud maintenance windows and expected failover behavior for Dedicated customers. (Owner: Marco Rivera, due 2026-07-06)\- Priming defaults: set adaptive priming as the default for hosted lanes in APAC for one-week trial. Metrics owners must validate cost delta and latency benefits. (Owner: Trevor Huang, due 2026-07-09)
- Cost offset play: enable a "pre-warm lane" surcharge toggle in console for customers who want guaranteed low tail latency (opt-in). Product to scope touchpoints next week. (Owner: Emilia Novak, product-hosted-api contact: @kevin)

Open questions and hypotheses to test next sprint
- Can we combine probabilistic pre-warm with dynamic model-variant routing so pre-warmed lanes use the same model variant customers were pinned to (avoid quality regressions)?
- Is there a better signal than short-session inter-arrival to drive priming decisions — e.g., correlation with external metrics (calendar events) or customer-specific seasonality?
- Does the adaptive floor (2m) hold across workloads with longer prefix reuse (embeddings-heavy customers)? We'll run a micro-experiment focusing on long-context embedding pipelines next week.

Action items (short list)
- Jin: implement pinned-capacity guardrail prototype + small e2e test (due 2026-07-07).\- Marco: create Console mockups for maintenance disclosure and pre-warm surcharge flow; coordinate with design (due 2026-07-06).\- Trevor: rollout adaptive priming default to 10% of hosted APAC lanes and capture cost/latency delta (due 2026-07-02).\- Emilia: escalate Dedicated customer list affected by Jun 27 maintenance and run CS follow-ups (due 2026-07-01).\- Aisha: consolidate experiment logs + metric dashboards and produce cleaned playbook doc for review (due 2026-07-09).

Notes to self / rough checklist
- Validate that warm cache retention TTLs still align across serving-runtime and dedicated images.
- Add a small heatmap export to the weekly report: per-region spare percentage by hour (easy win for ops page).
- Reconcile cost numbers for pre-warm lanes with finance to avoid surprises in invoice summaries.

Appendix — quick metric snapshots (rounded)
- APAC p95 latency (baseline week prior): 320ms\- APAC p95 latency (adaptive priming): 275ms\- Global coldstart error rate (baseline): 0.62%\- Global coldstart error rate (prob-prewarm 25%): 0.34%\- Fleet token-cost delta (week of experiment): +1.8% (aggregate across experiments)

Next sync
Quarterly-like priming/runbook sync on Tuesday 2026-07-07 16:00 UTC (owners and metrics leads). Please add topics to the meeting doc before EOD 2026-07-05.

If anything is missing or you want raw traces / aggregated dashboards attached, comment in the linked Slack thread or ping me directly.

-- Aisha
